proof_review.finding: Pass. Financed columns span exactly zero-cost payoffs with the positive-price unit bond. The simplex is compact and disjoint from the closed finite-dimensional zero-cost subspace. The minimum squared-distance residual is nonzero and orthogonal to that subspace; its feasible-segment derivative yields d_s >= ||d||^2 > 0. Bond normalization then prices every column. Sufficiency covers both nonzero nonnegative payoffs and negative-cost zero payoffs. No completeness or investor utility is silently assumed.

Pass. Full row rank makes the transpose kernel trivial. In the incomplete no-arbitrage case, small positive/negative null-space perturbations preserve strict positivity and quoted prices. The orthogonal residual of a nonreplicable claim changes its value under those extensions, proving claim-specific uniqueness iff replicability. Redundant holdings are correctly distinguished from state-price uniqueness.

Pass. The high-state digital family, strict endpoint exclusion and explicit sub/superhedge certificates are derived for the declared equal-spaced three-state market. No assertion that all incomplete-market endpoint bounds share this form. The changed-stock-price branch with a nonzero lower hedge also closes.

Pass. m=q/pi, E[m]=B, Q=q/B and unit-cost gross return pricing have consistent units. Changing positive physical probabilities at fixed traded prices changes m and physical moments without changing q or Q. Zero-cost excess payoffs are not called returns on zero capital.

Pass. The covariance identity and absolute Cauchy bound have correct signs and boundary cases. Equality requires perfect centered proportionality, with negative sign for a positive premium. The priced tight-bound payoff is actually replicated in this complete unrestricted market; an incomplete or constrained menu is not assumed to attain every point satisfying the moment inequality.

Pass. The Euler condition is restricted to increasing differentiable concave utility, positive consumption and feasible two-sided local trades. The one-sided buy-only derivative has the correct <= inequality. A constructed consumption kernel is explicitly separate from an aggregate equilibrium or empirical consumption calibration.

independent_calculation_method: Executed a separate read-only exact Fraction audit through stdin. Used determinant expansion over permutations and Cramer solutions for primal/dual pricing rather than the benchmark Gaussian solver; pairwise-state covariance sums rather than either supplied centered-moment or second-moment implementation; direct state-by-state initial/final cash certificates and an explicit numerical witness for the projection proof.
